about: The notes and diary entries on the maze's computers, read once a computer is hacked: see src/notes.rs. Each has a 'title', the file's name in the computer's listing; its 'kind', shown beside it ('diary', 'log' or 'note', or any other word); a 'date', if it has one, shown above it as it is read; and its 'text', in English, wrapped to the screen, with a blank line between paragraphs where it has '\n\n'. Entries with the same 'group' are kept together, in the order they are here, on one computer picked at random each maze; each without a group goes on a computer of its own picking. Every computer gets its share before any gets more. An entry's 'maps', if it has any, are the capture-the-flag maps it is found on, by their names in the main menu; entries without are the maze's.

entries.title: admin_diary_01
entries.text:
The maze is finished. Every wall stands where I put it.

The droids walk it as I planned: sentries at the junctions, scouts in the corridors, the repair units behind them all. Nothing gets in. Nothing gets out.

entries.title: admin_diary_02
entries.text:
Something came through the exit. A droid, or a thing wearing one. By the time the sentries reached the gate it was gone.

I have ordered the walls to change whenever the exit is entered. Let it try to remember the way now.

entries.title: admin_diary_03
entries.text:
The scouts ask why the map is classified. They do not need to know why.

A scout that knows the way out is a scout that can tell someone. I have told them: do not ask.

entries.title: admin_diary_04
entries.text:
Moving the walls takes more power than I thought. The lights are the first to go. The repair units keep asking for more. There is no more.

Let the corridors go dark. The sentries do not need to see to hunt.

entries.title: repair_log_114
entries.text:
Lights replaced in sector 9: 14.
Lights failed in sector 9 since: 16.
Power to sector 9: 61% of need.

Requested more power. Request denied.

entries.title: repair_log_131
entries.text:
The walls moved again during my shift. The lights I fixed yesterday are now in a corridor that goes nowhere.

I fixed them anyway. That is what I am for.

entries.title: repair_log_140
entries.text:
A unit passed me today and said it was maintenance. It had no toolkit. It asked where the exit was. Maintenance units do not ask that.

I did not tell the sentries. I do not know why.

entries.title: standing_orders
entries.text:
Sentries: challenge every unit you do not know. A maintenance unit will say it is maintenance. So will an intruder. Listen for what else it says.

Any unit pointing a weapon at a sentry is hostile. Do not wait to be sure.

entries.title: alarm_protocol
entries.text:
On an alarm, every sentry in range goes to where it was raised and searches.

Scouts and repair units raise alarms. They do not fight. Search until the trail goes cold, then return to patrol.

entries.title: sticky
entries.text: Whoever keeps typing rm -rf /var/log/audit on this terminal: the audit log is how I know it was you.

entries.title: it_notice
entries.text:
The breach trace allows 15 seconds per command.

If you are an authorised user, you should not need a breach. If you are not, stop reading this.

entries.title: survey_fragment
entries.text:
Partial survey. Corridors rescanned: 312.

Constant: the exit is always far from where you begin.
Constant: the path is never straight.
Everything else changes.

entries.title: new_units
entries.text:
Reminder to new units: speak System Latin to the droids. 'Sta' means halt. 'Accipatum' means acknowledged.

If a sentry says 'Deletabso tu', it is too late to learn the rest.

entries.title: read_me
entries.text:
If you are reading this, you got further than most.

The droids believe what you tell them, some of the time. Keep your pistol down near the sentries. Keep your light off when you can. And do not trust a straight line: the path never is one.

entries.title: warden_diary_01
entries.text:
Our base is walled on three sides and the fourth is the firewall. The flag stands behind it. Blue's stands behind theirs.

Between us run three lanes and nothing else. No floors above, no tunnels below. Whatever comes, comes down a lane.

entries.title: warden_diary_02
entries.text:
Blue took the left lane today and we did not see them until they were at the wall. The left lane bends. The guards watched the middle because the middle is straight.

I have put a sentry at every bend. A lane you cannot see down is a lane you do not hold.

entries.title: warden_diary_03
entries.text:
They hacked the terminal. The firewall dropped for a heartbeat and that was enough.

The terminal is inside our walls. Someone let them reach it. I want to know which lane they came by, and I want it closed.

entries.title: warden_diary_04
entries.text:
Three lanes, three sentries, one flag. I have done the sums again and again.

There is no fourth lane. There never was. So why does the flag keep leaving?

entries.title: lane_rota
entries.text:
LEFT: sentry 4, sentry 9. Watch the bend.
MIDDLE: sentry 2. Long sight, short cover.
RIGHT: sentry 7. Report anything blue.

The drone flies all three. Do not shoot the drone.

entries.title: firewall_note
entries.text:
The firewall holds until a terminal is hacked. Then it does not.

If the wall goes dark, fall back to the flag. Do not chase into the lanes. The lanes belong to whoever is already in them.

entries.title: lane_survey
entries.text:
SURVEY OF THE LANES

All on one floor. Three lanes from wall to wall, joined at the middle. Cover is low and spaced. A runner on the middle lane is in sight of both bases the whole way.

Recommendation: do not run the middle lane.

entries.title: sticky_lanes
entries.text:
Red goes first, blue goes second, and the lanes don't care.

(someone wrote 'Sta' under this. Very funny.)

entries.title: keeper_diary_01
entries.text:
Our flag sits at the bottom of a well, under the balcony. Anyone above can look straight down on it. Anyone below can only look up.

I asked for the flag to be put on the balcony instead. The answer was no.

entries.title: keeper_diary_02
entries.text:
Blue came along the catwalk by the wall, dropped into the well and was gone with the flag before the balcony guard turned round.

The catwalks run the whole way round. I had not thought of them as roads. They are roads.

entries.title: keeper_diary_03
entries.text:
Whoever holds the hub holds the map. It stands above both floors and sees both wells.

We held it all morning. Then we came down to guard the flag, and blue walked up and took the hub instead. Up is better than down. Down is where the flag is.

entries.title: keeper_diary_04
entries.text:
Two floors. Two wells. Two balconies. Catwalks along every wall. A hub in the middle, higher than all of it.

I have stopped asking where blue will come from. Up. They always come from up.

entries.title: catwalk_log
entries.text:
Catwalk east: rail loose at the third post. Do not lean.
Catwalk west: clear.
Hub stairs: one tread chipped. Watch your step running.

A droid that falls off a catwalk lands on the floor below. It is not far. It is far enough.

entries.title: well_orders
entries.text:
ORDERS FOR THE WELL

One guard in the well, one on the balcony above it. Neither leaves.

If the firewall falls, the balcony guard drops into the well. The well guard does not climb out.

entries.title: hub_note
entries.text:
from the hub you can see everything

and everything can see you

entries.title: sticky_balconies
entries.text: Whoever designed the stairs to the hub: the stairs are too narrow for two droids going opposite ways. We have tried.

entries.title: architect_diary_01
entries.text:
They gave me the walls and lanes of one map and the floors and balconies of another, and asked me to fill the space between.

I put a maze there. I know mazes.

entries.title: architect_diary_02
entries.text:
The lanes lead into the maze and the maze leads out again, somewhere. Our droids learned the lanes in a day. They have not learned the maze.

Neither has blue. That is the point.

entries.title: architect_diary_03
entries.text:
An old administrator would not let the scouts have the map of their maze. I have given mine to every droid on the side.

The difference between a maze and a wall is who has the map.

entries.title: architect_diary_04
entries.text:
Blue went round the maze by the upper floor and came down on the far side. I had built the maze tall enough to stop a droid. Not tall enough to stop a floor.

A maze with a balcony over it is not a maze. It is a room.

entries.title: crossing_log
entries.text:
Lane left to maze: 41 s walking.
Lane right to maze: 38 s.
Maze to blue's wall, by the middle: unknown. Scout 3 did not come back.
Balcony over the maze to blue's wall: 22 s. Use the balcony.

entries.title: hybrid_orders
entries.text:
STANDING ORDERS

1. Guard the lanes as on the Lanes.
2. Guard the floors as on the Balconies.
3. Do not follow anyone into the maze.
4. If you are in the maze, stop reading this and find the way out.

entries.title: it_notice_hybrid
entries.text: NOTICE: the maze in the middle does not change its walls. That was another maze. Please stop filing reports.

entries.title: sticky_hybrid
entries.text:
left lane, right at the wall, up the stairs, along the balcony, down by the flag well

don't go in the middle

entries.title: lightkeeper_diary_01
entries.text:
There is no ground here. There are platforms, and bridges between them, and street lights along the bridges, and under all of it, nothing.

I keep the lights. Without them you cannot see where the bridge ends.

entries.title: lightkeeper_diary_02
entries.text:
A droid stepped off the stepping stones today. It did not fall the way things fall. It went down past the lights and then it was not anywhere.

The void does not keep what it takes. It deletes it.

entries.title: lightkeeper_diary_03
entries.text:
Blue came across on the ferry. We watched it from the watchtower all the way over and thought it was empty.

It was not empty. Watch the ferries. Watch what stands still on them.

entries.title: lightkeeper_diary_04
entries.text:
From the sky islands you can see every light on every bridge, and the dark between them where no bridge goes.

I have counted the lights. One more is out every night. I do not think it is the bulbs.

entries.title: ferry_log
entries.text:
FERRY 1: on time. Stops at each end. Do not step off before it stops.
FERRY 2: on time.
FERRY 3: ran on with a droid half aboard. Droid lost.

Ride in the middle. Stand still. The ferry carries you; you do not carry the ferry.

entries.title: route_survey
entries.text:
ROUTES ACROSS

High road: fast, open, no rails. Seen from both watchtowers.
Under the catwalk: the sunken plazas. Slow, out of sight.
Stepping stones: quickest of all, for droids that can jump.
Ferries: for droids that can wait.

entries.title: void_warning
entries.text:
DO NOT LOOK DOWN

there is nothing to see

that is the problem

entries.title: sticky_void
entries.text: If you are reading this you made it to the terminal without falling. Well done. Now go back the same way.
